title: Soler: how things used to be in Cuba

sections.content: You know *soler* + infinitive from B1 Unit 5: it says that someone usually does something, and in the imperfect it means "used to". It is the natural tool to describe the habits of a whole society before a big change, as in Cuba before 1959.

items.spanish: Los trabajadores del azúcar solían trabajar solo durante la zafra.
items.english: The sugar workers used to work only during the harvest.

items.spanish: Los estudiantes solían reunirse y protestar contra el gobierno.
items.english: The students used to meet and protest against the government.

items.spanish: Antes de 1959 los gobiernos solían tener problemas de corrupción.
items.english: Before 1959 governments used to have problems of corruption.

items.spanish: Muchos turistas solían visitar La Habana.
items.english: Many tourists used to visit Havana.

sections.content: *Soler* is used almost only in the present (*suele*) and the imperfect (*solía*). Do not add a preposition: *solían trabajar*, not *solían a trabajar*. For one event that happened once, use the preterite instead: *Batista tomó el poder en 1952*.
